**C.** The Grand Chamber held in *Al-Adsani v. United Kingdom* (2001, 9–8) that granting Kuwait state immunity in the English courts did not violate Article 6(1), because the immunity rule pursued a legitimate aim and was proportionate, so it did not conflict with the right of access to a court. The Court also held that the prohibition of torture, though jus cogens, did not override state immunity in civil proceedings.

CONFIDENCE: 92
